A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BraInCoRL study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original NSD and BOLD5000 prediction experiments, model ablations, cortical visualizations, and natural-language prompt evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds alternative-metric evaluations, training-component ablations, and full-context results.

M1.justification: The transformer-generated voxelwise linear encoders, three-stage training, MSE objective, and logit-scaling procedure remain unchanged. The added CLS-token explanation clarifies implementation; alternative losses and removal of scaling are experimental controls rather than changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same NSD and BOLD5000 populations, natural-image encoding tasks, category-selective regions, and language-based cortical queries. The added experiments use existing subjects and datasets; increasing context size changes sample counts within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The ridge-regression, FsAverage, and fully trained reference comparisons are retained. V2 additionally evaluates L1 and hybrid-loss variants and a no-logit-scaling control against the proposed model in Figures S.29-S.30, extending the comparison set through internal variants.

E3.justification: Appendices A.14-A.19 substantially extend evaluation settings: Pearson and Spearman correlations for NSD S1, explained variance and Spearman correlation for BOLD5000 CSI1, direct conditioning on all 9,000 support images, and controlled checkpoint, loss, and scaling comparisons. These supplement the existing protocols rather than establish changes to the original data splits.

E4.justification: V1 already tests pretraining versus finetuning, image holdout, and support-set specificity. V2 separately examines the two pretraining stages, compares MSE, L1, and hybrid losses, and removes logit scaling to test its contribution. These additions substantially strengthen component-specific analysis, alongside evaluation at the full 9,000-image context.

E5.justification: Both versions display variability bands and report five-fold averaging for the retained BOLD5000 appendix evaluation. V2 provides no new run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions, or formal significance-testing procedures; its additional plots extend the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: The retained numerical tables and findings are unchanged, but V2 adds substantial results for alternative metrics and component controls. The new experiments show similar MSE/L1 performance, weaker hybrid-loss performance, and marked degradation without logit scaling. Table S.16 newly reports 9,000-context results, including S1 explained variance of 0.1667 against 0.1765 for the fully trained reference.

T1.justification: V1 states the logit-scaling rule in Equation 4 without deriving it. V2 Appendix A.4 adds an attention-entropy derivation using layer-normalized vector lengths and high-dimensional angle approximations. This is a focused mathematical addition motivating an existing component, rather than a new theoretical framework.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of data-efficient voxel encoding, adaptation without finetuning, generalization across subjects and scanning protocols, and interpretable language-based cortical mapping. The added evidence supports these claims without redefining their scientific scope.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the training stages as addressing complementary challenges and attributes the hybrid loss's weaker performance to constraints on response-magnitude prediction. It also discusses potential applications and resource-access/privacy limitations in Appendix A.1. The original limitations concerning static stimuli and dataset diversity remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a stated public code-and-model-weight link, specifies tokenwise input projection and CLS-token weight prediction, and clarifies random support/test-image sampling in Section 4.2. These are additional access and implementation disclosures; the reported hardware, optimizer, model sizes, and training budgets remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Llama 4 reference and identifies it as another use of attention scaling in Appendix A.4. The existing bibliography and positioning relative to brain encoders, meta-learning, and in-context learning otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are largely retained. V2 makes localized explanatory edits, corrects the context-token response notation, updates the conference footer, and expands and renumbers the appendix organization. It does not extensively rewrite the existing exposition.

P2.justification: V2 adds a substantial supplementary display suite comprising Figures S.23-S.30 and Table S.16 for the new evaluations and controls. Existing main figures and tables are resized or relocated, Figure 7 gains explained-variance axis labels, and Figure 3's caption clarifies its axes. The retained appendix displays preserve their content.

improvement.justification: V2 better supports previously untested design choices through loss and logit-scaling ablations, while alternative metrics and full-context evaluation strengthen the retained empirical conclusions. Implementation clarification and the stated code/model-weight link improve reproducibility information. These are focused gains over an already extensive study; the new assertion that the training-stage order is optimal exceeds what the checkpoint comparisons establish.
